subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the value of sin² 82½° − sin² 22½°.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.106 — from the book's separate "STAR QUESTIONS PLUS" bank, answer 165. That bank (book pp.98-111, answers 142-180) sits AFTER all the numbered chapters and is organised by chapter rather than forming part of any chapter's own inventory; it is authored into this unit because that is where the question belongs on the paper (founder decision 2026-08-22). SECTION: classed VSAQ on its length and shape. The bank prints no mark cut, so this classification is OURS. Printed appearances: TS 19. The awkward halves disappear the moment the difference-of-squares identity is used: the sum is 105° and the difference is 60°, both ordinary angles. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — the bank prints no [N Marks] tags anywhere. The shapes used follow the splits the book DOES print elsewhere: 1+1 for a 2-mark VSAQ (answers 100, 101 on book p.82), 1+1+1+1 or 1+2+1 for a 4-mark SAQ (answers 58, 59 on p.63 and 61 on p.64), and the granular split for a 7-mark LAQ (answer 32 on p.44). This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name each move in order.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Apply the difference of squares
steps.margin_note: First mark. sin²A − sin²B = sin(A+B) sin(A−B). The halves cancel: the sum is 105° and the difference is 60°.
lines: sin²A − sin²B = sin(A + B) sin(A − B)

recall.must_convey: That sin²A − sin²B = sin(A+B) sin(A−B) turns the expression into sin 105° · sin 60°.
accept: use sin squared A minus sin squared B equals sin of A plus B into sin of A minus B giving sin one oh five into sin sixty
the sum is one hundred and five and the difference is sixty
the halves cancel in both the sum and the difference
A plus B one oh five, A minus B sixty
apply the difference of squares identity

steps.why: Both halves land on whole degrees — 82½ + 22½ = 105 and 82½ − 22½ = 60. That is why this identity is the intended route.
common_mistakes: Using cos²A − cos²B, which has an extra minus sign.

steps.label: Expand sin 105°
steps.margin_note: Second mark. 105° = 60° + 45°, so use the sine addition formula, then multiply by sin 60° = √3/2.

accept: sin one oh five is sin of sixty plus forty five which gives root three plus one over two root two, and multiplying by root three over two gives the answer
split one oh five into sixty plus forty five
the value is root three into root three plus one over four root two
one oh five ni sixty plus forty five ga rasi expand cheyyali

steps.why: 105° is not a standard angle, but it splits into two that are. Choosing 60° + 45° rather than 30° + 75° keeps both parts standard.
common_mistakes: Using 105° = 45° + 60° but mixing up which is which in the formula.
